findings.issue_text: [BUG] In flusher.py join() (~line 355), when the deadline expires while waiting on process N, processes N+1…M never get terminate() called because terminate() happens after each process's inner wait loop and the loop breaks on remaining_time <= 0, leaving orphaned spawned flusher processes holding Redis connections and Kafka producers alive after parent exit

[ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard (~line 128) is dead code: nothing in the diff calls it, and if invoked it starts a new process for the shard's group without killing the old one, leaking a duplicate flusher — should be deleted

[ADVISORY] Default behavior change in factory.py:41 / flusher.py __init__: flusher_processes=None maps to max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards) (one process per shard), whereas pre-diff code ran exactly one flusher process; direct constructors without the new kwarg silently get N spawn processes each with its own SpansBuffer, Redis pool, and producer

[ADVISORY] Metric tag key drift in flusher.py:197 vs :200: the produce-timing timer uses tags={"shards": shard_tag} while segment_size_bytes and flusher_unhealthy use tags={"shard": ...}, so dashboards/alerts keyed on shard miss the wait_produce timer metric

[ADVISORY] In test_consumer.py:60-62, the new time.sleep(0.1) intended to give flusher threads time to process is monkeypatched away globally (monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)), so it is a no-op and the promised wait never happens, meaning per-process race coverage is not actually exercised

[ADVISORY] flusher_processes was inserted as a positional parameter before produce_to_pipe in factory.py:41-42, changing the positional signature of the public constructor; existing callers passing produce_to_pipe positionally now bind it to flusher_processes, causing TypeError or silently ignored pipe — the new kwarg should be appended after existing parameters

[BUG] Inconsistent tag keys in flusher.py main(): spans.buffer.flusher.produce uses tag key "shard" while spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce uses "shards", so queries grouping by shard silently drop the wait_produce series

[ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard is dead code; if ever called it would restart a process without killing the old one and without incrementing process_restarts, bypassing the MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS guard and enabling an unbounded-restart loop with zombie processes

[ADVISORY] No tests exercise the new health-monitoring path (_ensure_processes_alive hang detection, MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS RuntimeError, kill/restart via _create_process_for_shards); both new tests only assert process-count and shard-distribution on the happy path

[ADVISORY] Behavior change from one shared buffer to N per-process buffers is unverified: record_stored_segments() now runs N times on N disjoint buffers with no assertion that per-buffer aggregation equals the old all-shards recording

[ADVISORY] Memory-info aggregation now sums get_memory_info() across N SpansBuffer instances; if it returns service-level memory, summing inflates used and can trip max_memory_percentage early, and no test covers the memory-backpressure branch

[BUG] join() timeout regression: when the deadline expires mid-wait, the break exits the outer for loop so subsequent processes are never terminate()d and remain running as orphans holding Redis connections and producer handles past shutdown

[ADVISORY] --flusher-processes is a CLI option only with no options-entry or feature flag; the same command with and without the flag produces different fan-out with no operator visibility or documented rollback other than a deploy

[ADVISORY] CLAUDE.md:452 contains unrelated documentation change (hasattr vs isinstance union-checking guidance) with no connection to the span buffer multiprocess enhancement, causing scope drift and diff bloat

[ADVISORY] The `buffer` argument passed by the factory is used only to read `buffer.assigned_shards`; the flusher constructs entirely new `SpansBuffer(shards)` instances per process and ignores the injected buffer, silently decoupling the factory's buffer from the flusher and risking divergence when `SpansBuffer` semantics change

[ADVISORY] Dead code: `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard)` has no call site anywhere in the diff or codebase; its comment says "restart that process" while doing a full create, misleading readers hunting for the restart path

[BUG] Inconsistent metrics tag keys: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` uses tag `shard` while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses tag `shards`, so dashboards/alerts slicing by `shard` silently drop all `wait_produce` series

[BUG] The kill path in `_ensure_processes_alive` is guarded by `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, but spawn-context processes are `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` instances which are not subclasses of the default-context `Process`, so in real multiprocess deployments the crashed/hung flusher process is never killed before its replacement spawns, leaving a zombie holding the old shard's Redis leases/connections — a regression from the pre-diff unconditional `self.process.kill()`

[ADVISORY] Coverage gap in `test_flusher_processes_limit`: no test exercises the new per-process health path (`_ensure_processes_alive` hang/crash detection, per-process restart counters, or the `RuntimeError` after `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS`), so a regression in the restart/kill logic ships undetected
[ADVISORY] `test_basic` uses a fixed `time.sleep(0.1)` to give flusher threads time, making the test depend on wall-clock racing against a background thread and prone to intermittent CI flakes

[BUG] In process/flusher.py:247-259, when produce_to_pipe is set, a hung flusher thread is detected via healthy_since but the kill is skipped due to the isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard, so the old thread keeps polling the same Redis shard keys while _create_process_for_shards starts a replacement thread for those exact shards, resulting in two concurrent consumers of the same shards, duplicate segment reads, and spans produced to Kafka twice with no downstream dedup

[ADVISORY] Parallel duplication of shard-assignment state: the factory holds the full-shard buffer (writer side) while the flusher builds per-process SpansBuffer(shards) copies from a one-shot snapshot of buffer.assigned_shards, with no single source of truth for shard→process mapping; future mutations of shard assignment outside create_with_partitions leave the writer's full buffer and flusher's per-shard buffers silently diverged, so segments never flush

[ADVISORY] Conflicting defaults for the same knob: the CLI default is flusher_processes=1 but the factory/SpanFlusher default max_processes=None resolves to one process per shard, so programmatic construction of ProcessSpansStrategyFactory without flusher_processes silently deploys N spawn processes where code previously ran 1, causing unbounded process fan-out for code paths bypassing the CLI

[ADVISORY] Metric tag-key drift within the same loop: spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes use tags={"shard": shard_tag} while spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce uses tags={"shards": shard_tag}, so dashboards/alerts grouping on shard silently miss wait_produce data with split series from the same flush cycle

[ADVISORY] Dead code: _create_process_for_shard (singular) is never called anywhere in the diff since restarts go through _create_process_for_shards; it also creates a new SpansBuffer per call without removing the old process's entry, so if invoked it would double-register a shard's buffer

[ADVISORY] No test coverage for the new multi-process health/restart machinery: per-process healthy_since, restart counting, the RuntimeError at MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS, and per-process backpressure aggregation in submit() are unexercised since no added tests kill or hang a process, so a regression in the restart path or backpressure MessageRejected ships green

[ADVISORY] Stand-in guard in test_consumer.py:60-63: monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None) patches time.sleep globally, so the test's own time.sleep(0.1) meant to give flusher threads time to process is a no-op; the test passes or fails on thread-scheduling luck without deterministically verifying the drift→flush→produce ordering

[ADVISORY] submit() now loops for buffer in self.buffers.values() calling buffer.record_stored_segments(), so a single submit on the consumer's poll path issues one Redis-side bookkeeping call per flusher process instead of one per consumer, multiplying Redis bookkeeping load by flusher_processes at high submit rates

[BUG] flusher.py:53: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` silently changes the default deployment envelope from one flusher process to one process per shard; deployments not passing the new CLI flag spawn len(assigned_shards) processes (e.g. 32 processes for 32 partitions), causing a multiplicative jump in processes, Redis clients, and metric cardinality, with no feature flag or option to disable. The CLI default of 1 only covers the `ingest-transactions` entrypoint; other instantiation paths of ProcessSpansStrategyFactory inherit the unbounded default.

[BUG] flusher.py:124/268: The diff splits one shared buffer into per-shard SpansBuffers, but `submit()` still routes each incoming partition message through `record_stored_segments()` on all buffers (`for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()`), so each shard-buffer records segments for shards it does not own; drift/backpressure bookkeeping no longer reflects the intended per-shard signal, silently changing the single-buffer backpressure semantics.

[BUG] flusher.py:201 vs 184: Inconsistent metric tag key — `produce` and `segment_size_bytes` use tag `"shard"` while `wait_produce` uses `"shards"` for the same value; dashboards/alerts aggregating by the `shard` tag silently drop `wait_produce` data.

[ADVISORY] CLAUDE.md:448: Unrelated CLAUDE.md style-guide edit (hasattr/isinstance example) included in this span-buffer infrastructure PR, muddying git-blame/revert granularity and associating a doc-policy change with a consumer-ops behavior change.

[ADVISORY] flusher.py:145: `_create_process_for_shard` is dead code with zero call sites; the per-shard restart path it implies was replaced by full per-process restart in `_ensure_processes_alive`, and it duplicates `process_to_shards_map` logic in a second hand-maintained traversal.

[ADVISORY] test_consumer.py:60: `test_basic` changed from deterministic to timing-dependent — `@pytest.mark.django_db` was silently upgraded to `transaction=True` and a `time.sleep(0.1)` added to give flusher threads time, risking CI flakes and changing test isolation guarantees.

[ADVISORY] flusher.py:218: Health-check loop adds a silent `continue` branch for falsy entries in `self.processes`, but nothing in the diff ever stores a falsy value in that dict — a guard for an unreachable state that misleads future health-check changes.

Restart logic appends new processes without clearing old entries
`flusher_processes or len(...)` semantics mishandles `0`
`isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` check may be wrong given the actual `SpawnProcess` type
`process_restarts` dict is accessed across threads without synchronization

[BUG] The per-process wait loop in flusher.py (~line 335, `join`) `break`s when `remaining_time <= 0` without terminating that process or any subsequent ones — on a join timeout, one or more spawned flusher processes are left running past the consumer's shutdown, potentially hanging shutdown or orphaning processes that keep polling Redis/producing to Kafka after teardown.

[BUG] `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` at flusher.py:196 uses tag key "shards" while sibling metrics in the same method use "shard", causing wait_produce to land in a different time series family and dashboards/alerting keyed on the shard tag to miss wait_produce data.

[ADVISORY] `test_flusher_processes_limit` is a mirror test asserting constructor bookkeeping rather than behavior — `assert sum(len(shards) ...) == 4` is tautological; nothing verifies segments actually flow through both processes, that each process only flushes its assigned shards, or that commits/messages are produced correctly under the split.

[ADVISORY] The health-monitoring half of the diff — per-process hang detection, `no_process_{exitcode}` cause, `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` RuntimeError, `process.kill()` + restart — has zero test coverage; neither modified test file triggers a crash, hang, or restart.

[ADVISORY] Config-default skew: the CLI option defaults `flusher_processes=1` while the programmatic/factory default is `None` (→ one process per shard), and no test covers either default path.

[BUG] In `_ensure_processes_alive`, the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard means thread-backed flushers (the `produce_to_pipe is not None` path) are never killed on restart; the zombie thread and replacement thread both poll the same Redis shards, producing duplicate spans to Kafka, and `self.processes[process_index]` overwrites the zombie making it untracked and un-killable.

[BUG] In `join`, the `break` after `remaining_time <= 0` exits the for loop, so all remaining flusher processes are never terminated or waited on — orphaned processes keep polling Redis and produce into an already-closed `next_step` pipeline after shutdown.

[ADVISORY] If `buffer.assigned_shards` is empty, `num_processes` is 0, no flusher processes are created, and spans written to Redis are never flushed — silent unflushed data accumulation with no guard or log.
[ADVISORY] `_create_process_for_shard` is dead code with no call site; it misleads the next maintainer expecting per-shard restart semantics — delete it or wire it up.

[ADVISORY] Inconsistent metric tag key: `"shard"` used in `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` / `flusher_unhealthy` but `"shards"` in `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce`, splitting metric series and breaking per-shard health monitoring.

[ADVISORY] `SpanFlusher.main` static entry point gained a new required positional `shards` arg inserted before `stopped`; out-of-tree callers using old positional order silently misbind arguments and crash on first use.

[BUG] In `_ensure_processes_alive` (flusher.py ~245), the restart path only terminates the old worker when it's a multiprocessing.Process; in threaded mode a process reported with cause="hang" is never killed, so two concurrent flusher threads poll and flush the same Redis shards, producing duplicate spans.buffer Kafka payloads, and process_restarts increments forever until MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS is crossed

[ADVISORY] In `submit` (flusher.py ~265), `record_stored_segments()` is now called once per shard-buffer per invocation instead of once, causing N× Redis calls per batch proportional to --flusher-processes, a hot-path latency/Redis-load regression

[ADVISORY] `--flusher-processes` default=1 in src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py (~432) silently collapses consumers from one flusher process per shard to a single process handling all shards on deploy, reducing span-flush throughput and causing rising Redis span-buffer memory / flusher.backpressure rejections

[ADVISORY] Dead guard `if not process: continue` (flusher.py ~243) is unreachable since self.processes values are always live SpawnProcess/Thread objects, obscuring real failure semantics handled by is_alive()
[ADVISORY] Dead code: `_create_process_for_shard` (flusher.py ~125) has no call sites in the diff, creating two near-identical creation entry points that will drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a clear default behavior change: `SpanFlusher.__init__` now sets `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`, so when `max_processes` is not provided it becomes `len(assigned_shards)` (effectively one process per shard). Pre-diff, the flusher created exactly one background process/thread via `_create_process()`. The new implementation also creates a new `SpansBuffer(shards)` per process in `_create_process_for_shards`, so direct callers who don’t pass the new kwarg will silently get multiple processes and multiple buffers (and corresponding per-process resources) instead of one. This is a concrete, diff-grounded concern about unintended resource/behavior changes, but not provably a correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher`, `_create_process_for_shard` is defined but not referenced anywhere in the diff (no callers shown), so it is effectively dead code. The implementation does indeed call `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` without killing/terminating any existing process for that `process_index`, and it does not update `self.process_restarts[...]` (unlike `_ensure_processes_alive`, which increments and enforces `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS`). If this method were ever used, it could leave the old process running and bypass the restart guard. However, since the diff does not show it being called, this is a maintainability/latent-risk issue rather than a currently verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate correctly notes that time.sleep in the test is ineffective because it was monkeypatched to a no-op, matching the golden issue about the intended wait/synchronization not actually occurring and needing a different approach or restoring sleep.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` at flusher.py:196 uses tag key "shards" while sibling metrics in the same method use "shard", causing wait_produce to land in a different time series family and dashboards/alerting keyed on the shard tag to miss wait_produce data.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main`, sibling metrics use tag key `"shard"` (e.g. `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`), but `wait_produce` is emitted with `tags={"shards": shard_tag}`. This inconsistency is visible in the diff and will split the time series by tag schema, so shard-keyed dashboards/alerts would miss `wait_produce` data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `test_flusher_processes_limit` is a mirror test asserting constructor bookkeeping rather than behavior — `assert sum(len(shards) ...) == 4` is tautological; nothing verifies segments actually flow through both processes, that each process only flushes its assigned shards, or that commits/messages are produced correctly under the split.

adjudication.rationale: The new test `test_flusher_processes_limit` (in `tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py`) only asserts internal bookkeeping fields created in `SpanFlusher.__init__`—`len(flusher.processes)`, `flusher.max_processes`, `flusher.num_processes`, and that `process_to_shards_map` contains 4 shards total. The `total_shards == 4` check is effectively guaranteed by the initialization loop over `buffer.assigned_shards` and does not validate runtime behavior (e.g., that flushing/producing happens correctly per shard group, that multiple processes/threads actually process their assigned shards, or that outputs/commits reflect the split). This is a concrete, diff-grounded test-quality concern rather than a functional defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] No test exercises the multiprocessing spawn path: both tests construct the flusher with `produce_to_pipe=messages.append`, forcing `make_process = threading.Thread`, so `self.mp_context.Process`, pickling of `shard_buffer`/`shards`/`mp_context.Value`s under spawn, and the real `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` kill/terminate branches never run in tests — the first execution of the spawn path is production.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in the diff: SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards picks `make_process = self.mp_context.Process` only when `self.produce_to_pipe is None`, otherwise it uses `threading.Thread`. All added/modified tests construct the flusher with a non-None `produce_to_pipe` (e.g. `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory(..., produce_to_pipe=messages.append)` in `test_basic` and `test_flusher_processes_limit`, and `produce_to_pipe=append` in `test_flusher.py`), so they exclusively exercise the thread path. As a result, the real multiprocessing spawn path (pickling `SpansBuffer(shards)`/`shards`/`mp_context.Value`s and the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` kill/terminate branches) is not covered by tests in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The health-monitoring half of the diff — per-process hang detection, `no_process_{exitcode}` cause, `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` RuntimeError, `process.kill()` + restart — has zero test coverage; neither modified test file triggers a crash, hang, or restart.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new health-monitoring/restart behavior in `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive()` (per-process hang detection via `process_healthy_since`, `no_process_{exitcode}` cause, `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` RuntimeError, `Process.kill()` + `_create_process_for_shards()` restart). The updated/new tests (`test_basic`, `test_flusher_processes_limit`, and the modified assertion in `test_flusher`) only validate normal operation (message flush, process-count limiting, and that some backpressure flag is set). None of them simulate a dead process (`is_alive() == False`), an unhealthy timestamp exceeding `max-unhealthy-seconds`, or repeated restarts to hit the RuntimeError path, so the new monitoring/restart logic is untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `_create_process_for_shard` (singular) at flusher.py:139-144 is dead code: nothing calls it, and calling it would re-create a process group and re-bind `self.processes[process_index]` without killing the old process, leaking the old process.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard` is defined (it just finds a `process_index` and calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`), but nothing in the shown code calls `_create_process_for_shard` (restarts are done via `_ensure_processes_alive` -> `_create_process_for_shards`). Also, `_create_process_for_shards`/`_create_process_for_shards` creates and starts a new process/thread and then overwrites `self.processes[process_index]` without terminating the previous one; the only termination logic exists in `_ensure_processes_alive` before it calls `_create_process_for_shards`. So the finding about dead code and the risk of leaking a process if it were called is grounded, but since it’s unused in this diff it’s more of a maintainability/latent-risk issue than an immediately verifiable bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Config-default skew: the CLI option defaults `flusher_processes=1` while the programmatic/factory default is `None` (→ one process per shard), and no test covers either default path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a CLI option `--flusher-processes` with `default=1` in `ingest_transactions_options()` (src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py), while the factory signature defaults `flusher_processes: int | None = None` (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py) and `SpanFlusher` interprets `None` as `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` via `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py). That is a real default-behavior skew between CLI and programmatic construction. Tests added cover an explicit non-default (`flusher_processes=2`) but do not assert/verify the intended behavior for either default (`None` meaning per-shard, or CLI default 1); `test_basic` uses the factory default but does not check process/shard mapping outcomes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In `_ensure_processes_alive`, the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard means thread-backed flushers (the `produce_to_pipe is not None` path) are never killed on restart; the zombie thread and replacement thread both poll the same Redis shards, producing duplicate spans to Kafka, and `self.processes[process_index]` overwrites the zombie making it untracked and un-killable.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that when `produce_to_pipe is not None`, `_create_process_for_shards` creates a `threading.Thread` (not a `multiprocessing.Process`). In `_ensure_processes_alive`, on an unhealthy flusher (including the `hang` path where `process.is_alive()` is still true but `healthy_since` is stale), the restart logic only attempts to kill the worker under `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.kill()`. For threads, this does nothing, and the code then unconditionally calls `_create_process_for_shards(...)`, starting a replacement thread and overwriting `self.processes[process_index]`. The original thread can remain alive and continue polling/producing for the same `shards`, creating the duplicate/untracked worker scenario described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In `join`, the `break` after `remaining_time <= 0` exits the for loop, so all remaining flusher processes are never terminated or waited on — orphaned processes keep polling Redis and produce into an already-closed `next_step` pipeline after shutdown.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join`, the loop over `self.processes` computes `remaining_time` and does `break` when `remaining_time <= 0` (new code in `join`). That exits the *entire* `for process_index, process in self.processes.items()` loop, so any later processes are neither waited on nor `terminate()`d by the subsequent per-process cleanup. This can leave some flusher processes still alive after `join(timeout=...)` returns.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] If `buffer.assigned_shards` is empty, `num_processes` is 0, no flusher processes are created, and spans written to Redis are never flushed — silent unflushed data accumulation with no guard or log.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`. If `buffer.assigned_shards` is empty, both become 0, `process_to_shards_map` is `{}`, and `_create_processes()` creates no workers. Subsequent health/backpressure checks iterate over empty dicts (`self.processes`, `self.buffers`), so nothing logs/raises, leaving the flusher step operationally inert. This is a behavior change from the prior code which always started one process via `_create_process()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `_create_process_for_shard` is dead code with no call site; it misleads the next maintainer expecting per-shard restart semantics — delete it or wire it up.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, the method `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` is introduced but there is no call site shown in the diff. The restart logic that is actually used is `_ensure_processes_alive()` which calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` directly. As-is, `_create_process_for_shard` is unused/dead code and could mislead maintainers into thinking per-shard restarts are implemented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Inconsistent metric tag key: `"shard"` used in `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` / `flusher_unhealthy` but `"shards"` in `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce`, splitting metric series and breaking per-shard health monitoring.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows inconsistent metric tag keys: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` use `shard`, while `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `shards`. Additionally, `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` is tagged with `{"cause": cause, "shard": shard}`. This inconsistency will split metric series across different tag keys and undermine per-shard dashboards/alerts, but it does not directly break runtime behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `SpanFlusher.main` static entry point gained a new required positional `shards` arg inserted before `stopped`; out-of-tree callers using old positional order silently misbind arguments and crash on first use.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `SpanFlusher.main` signature from `main(buffer, stopped, current_drift, ...)` to `main(buffer, shards, stopped, current_drift, ...)`, adding a new required positional `shards` argument inserted before `stopped`. This is a backwards-incompatible API change: any external/out-of-tree code still calling `SpanFlusher.main` with the old positional ordering would misbind arguments (e.g., `stopped` passed as `shards`) and likely fail at runtime. In-tree call sites shown in the diff were updated to pass `shards` explicitly, so it’s not a demonstrated in-repo crash, but it is a concrete compatibility risk introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In `_ensure_processes_alive` (flusher.py ~245), the restart path only terminates the old worker when it's a multiprocessing.Process; in threaded mode a process reported with cause="hang" is never killed, so two concurrent flusher threads poll and flush the same Redis shards, producing duplicate spans.buffer Kafka payloads, and process_restarts increments forever until MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS is crossed

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards`, when `produce_to_pipe` is provided the worker is a `threading.Thread` (see `make_process = threading.Thread`). In `_ensure_processes_alive`, the restart path only attempts to kill the worker if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, and otherwise just starts a new worker for the same `shards` via `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`. This means a hung thread cannot be terminated and a new thread will be started for the same shard set, so if the old thread later unblocks you can have two concurrent flusher threads polling/flushing the same Redis shards (duplicate production risk). The specific claim that `process_restarts` will “increment forever” is overstated because `healthy_since` is reset before restart and shared, but the unkillable-thread + duplicate-work risk is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In `submit` (flusher.py ~265), `record_stored_segments()` is now called once per shard-buffer per invocation instead of once, causing N× Redis calls per batch proportional to --flusher-processes, a hot-path latency/Redis-load regression

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `submit()` from calling `self.buffer.record_stored_segments()` once to iterating `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()` (flusher.py, ~264). `self.buffers` is populated with one `SpansBuffer` per flusher process in `_create_process_for_shards`, so this becomes O(num_processes) calls per `submit()` instead of O(1). The finding’s core concern (extra calls proportional to `--flusher-processes` / `max_processes`) is supported by the diff, though it is per *process buffer* (which may cover multiple shards), not strictly “per shard-buffer.” This is a performance/load regression concern, not a correctness defect, and the diff alone cannot prove these calls are Redis-heavy, but the increased call count is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `--flusher-processes` default=1 in src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py (~432) silently collapses consumers from one flusher process per shard to a single process handling all shards on deploy, reducing span-flush throughput and causing rising Redis span-buffer memory / flusher.backpressure rejections

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `--flusher-processes` click option with `default=1` (src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py) and wires it through `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory(..., flusher_processes=...)` into `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)` (factory.py/flusher.py). In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`, so a default of 1 will force a single flusher process to handle all assigned shards, bypassing the new “one process per shard” parallelism the refactor otherwise enables. However, the finding’s framing as a deploy regression (“collapses from one per shard”) and the asserted Redis/backpressure impact aren’t directly verifiable from the diff alone; it’s a performance/config-default concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Dead guard `if not process: continue` (flusher.py ~243) is unreachable since self.processes values are always live SpawnProcess/Thread objects, obscuring real failure semantics handled by is_alive()

adjudication.rationale: The cited guard exists (`for process_index, process in self.processes.items(): if not process: continue`), and based on the diff `self.processes` is only ever populated with a started `multiprocessing.Process` or `threading.Thread` in `_create_process_for_shards`, never with `None`/falsy values. So it is effectively dead/redundant, but removing it would not change behavior; this is a minor cleanup/style nit rather than a verifiable defect or important review issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Dead code: `_create_process_for_shard` (flusher.py ~125) has no call sites in the diff, creating two near-identical creation entry points that will drift

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, the diff adds a new helper method `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` that searches `process_to_shards_map` and calls `_create_process_for_shards(...)`, but there are no references/call sites to `_create_process_for_shard` anywhere in the shown diff. The live restart path in `_ensure_processes_alive` directly calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`. This makes `_create_process_for_shard` currently dead code and introduces an extra, near-duplicate process-creation entry point that can drift over time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Inconsistent metric tag key: `wait_produce` uses tag "shards" while `flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` use "shard", fragmenting the metric space so per-shard wait-time can't be correlated with produce-time

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main`, the metric tags are inconsistent: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` use the key `shard`, but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `shards`. This will split the metric series by different tag keys and makes it harder/impossible to correlate wait time vs produce time per shard group in dashboards/alerts, but it doesn't directly break runtime behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` (flusher.py ~52) treats an explicit flusher_processes=0 from the CLI as unset, silently falling back to one-process-per-shard (the maximum count) with no log or error

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` will treat an explicitly provided `max_processes=0` as falsy and replace it with `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`. The new CLI option (`click.Option(... type=int, default=1)`) does not constrain against 0, so `--flusher-processes 0` is plausible and would be silently ignored, potentially spawning one process per shard instead of respecting the user-provided value.
